thread:
katie: Starting staged rollout v3.2.0 -> 10% -> 30% over next 20m, EU region first. change window 22:00-23:00 UTC. pinging ops for go/no-go.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: v3.2.0 -> traffic 10% (eu-west). Canary instances: model-a-qa x12. CI: green. Links: https://ci.redwood/integrations/3321
josh: saw a small increase in p95 on the heatmap right after shift, watching.
tao: can you paste the heatmap snapshot?
katie: attaching quick screengrab in thread (img).
amanda: noticing KV cache fill on a subset of nodes, maybe cache warmup causing p95 bump.
ops-sre: taking a look at pod logs, seeing repeated WARNs about cache eviction for model-a-qa.
josh: magnitude is ~80ms p95 increase on eu-west for tail requests, overall success rate unchanged.
katie: is this transient from warmup or a real regression that will affect 30%?
ops-sre: initial read suggests warmup, but it's concentrated on one instance set behind the canary group (kernel mismatch). recommending hold at 10% until we confirm.
deploy-bot: Traffic shift paused by ops-sre (reason: canary p95 spike). Current traffic: 10% -> HOLD.
ta0: @tao typo in handle — tagging correctly: @tao.
tao: on it, checking kernel/quantization flags. quick grep: on three nodes, runtime shows mismatched fused-kernel build (v2.1 vs v2.0).
amanda: that explains the eviction pattern. If we pin to 2.0 kernel or remove those nodes from canary, we should be fine.
josh: agree. options: A) roll back those nodes from canary (safe) B) pin v3.2.0 to runtime v2.0 temporarily C) abort rollout and rollback to v3.1.4.
katie: ops opinion? we want minimal blast radius and fast recovery.
ops-sre: prefer option A (drain offending nodes from canary and retry shift to 30%). If draining takes >5m, fallback to B. Avoid full rollback if possible.
tao: can script node drain now. running: ```for node in node-23 node-24 node-29; do kubectl cordon $node && kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; done```
ops-sre: drain started. ETA ~3m.
deploy-bot: Drain hooks in progress. Canary group updated to exclude node-23, node-24, node-29. Health: passing.
josh: heatmap re-checking... p95 trending down, ~20ms delta now.
katie: quick pulse: are we comfortable to proceed to 30%? vote: :thumbsup: go / :thumbsdown: hold
amanda: :thumbsup: go (after drain look stable)
tao: :thumbsup: go (kernel mismatch addressed for canary)
ops-sre: :thumbsup: go (we'll keep close watch and alert on >50ms p95 drift)
josh: :thumbsdown: hold for 2m extra to ensure KV cache stabilizes (super cautious)
katie: call: we wait 2m then proceed. moving to 12m checkpoint then 30%.
deploy-bot: Resuming traffic shift: 10% -> 30% over 4m. Escalation policy: if p95 > +40ms or error rate >0.5% -> auto-pause and revert.
(2m pass)
josh: extra 2m looks clean, p95 near baseline. I'm good.
katie: consensus reached: proceed. executing final shift.
deploy-bot: Shift complete: 30% traffic -> success. Canary group healthy.
amanda: sanity checks: no new WARNs, cache hit-rate improving.
ops-sre: monitoring dashboard pinned to release lane. will keep 30m elevated sampling.
katie: filing release note snippet and action items: - pin canary kernel to v2.0 until fleet reprovision (TODO: infra ticket) - add deploy check to verify kernel parity pre-shift - incident ticket created for audit.
ops-sre: incident-4567 opened: "Canary kernel mismatch causing p95 bump". Assigned: infra-team.
josh: closing loop: no rollback needed. recommend postmortem blameless note and update rollout playbook to include kernel parity gate.
katie: thanks all. closing thread but will keep watch until end of change window. :white_check_mark: 
ops-sre: note for SRE oncall: if we see >2 consecutive spikes in 10m window escalate to SEV.
deploy-bot: Note: automated metric snapshots saved to https://logs.redwood/releases/4725012345/snapshots
katie: ack. good job team.
